title: Kerala Private Bus Operators Announce Indefinite Strike From November 3

tea.why: Private bus operators in Kerala are striking over financial losses linked to the state-run Priyadarshini scheme.
tea.want: Operators demand compensation for scheme losses, increased minimum fares, and implementation of commission recommendations.
tea.changed: Oct 27: Joint committee of bus owners announced an indefinite strike starting November 3 following failed talks with the Transport Minister.

summary: Private bus operators in Kerala have announced an indefinite statewide strike starting November 3, following a joint meeting held in Palakkad. According to news reports, six bus owners' associations decided on the action after accusing the state government of failing to address mounting financial losses allegedly caused by the Priyadarshini scheme, which offers free travel for women and transgender persons on ordinary KSRTC buses. The operators claimed that discussions with Transport Minister C P John on October 10 yielded no favourable outcome. Their demands include compensation for revenue losses, raising the minimum bus fare to Rs 15, student concession adjustments, and implementation of recommendations submitted by a special commission appointed on September 2. As of reporting, no official response or resolution from the government authorities has been detailed in the sources regarding the impending shutdown.
demands: Compensation for losses linked to the Priyadarshini scheme
Increase the minimum bus fare to Rs 15
Fix student concession fares at 50 per cent of regular tickets
Extend free travel facility for women to private buses with government reimbursement
Implement recommendations made by the special commission appointed on September 2
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Private bus operators in Palakkad announced an indefinite strike starting November 3 over financial losses.
